root_draft.speaker: agent
root_draft.text: Miasma is a stinking, beautiful nursery at the meeting of river and dying salt sea. Its crowded channels and rainbow growth offer hope in a place that is still dangerous: irregular surges move the salt line, leave young behind, and replenish the salvage caught in the roots. The colony must live with that changing shore, read what the brine has reached, and choose where to put its labour. A water-bound warden mother can hear young she cannot reach; people can return them and earn her tolerance, or sell them for a fortune and lose that relationship for good. Young that choose the colony can do useful work in the water and may inherit a smaller, weaker watch when she dies; her age must be apparent before that loss. Rot becomes electricity in decay cells, whose spent beds take corpses down to bones and named skulls and, with Cuisine, grow food. Silt and salt become attar for art and old scars. Ordinary disease remains dangerous, but surviving it here can leave a lasting change. The scuttlers, composters, predators and harmless blooms make this a living, crowded delta rather than a sequence of unrelated rewards. These connected promises need separate proofs and a demonstration of how they meet in an ordinary colony.

asks.title: The place the root has to describe
asks.picture: A small colony settles beside a filthy channel. The flowers are lovely, the next surge leaves a crying young beyond its mother's water, and that evening the colony has to choose between rescue, salvage and keeping its power running.
asks.picture_kind: written thought experiment, not a capture, mock image or staged game
asks.text: Which part of that day makes this Miasma to you, and where does the proposed root tell the wrong story?
asks.decision: Root's organising player promise and any correction to our proposed paragraph.
asks.why: F1/F2. The experience sentence is already yours; my longer paragraph could still make a crowded nursery sound like a collection of profitable chores.
asks.guess: The changing shore and the mother unable to reach her young are the heart; rot, beauty and salvage make living there worthwhile.
asks.tree_change: If the relationship leads, put the nursery decision first in the root and derive its central interaction from it. If learning to live with the moving shore leads, lead with siting, preparation and aftermath. If the working delta leads, centre the daily resource loop. Every built capability keeps coverage; a correction rewrites dependent promises. Silence leaves root null.

asks.title: The first demonstration
asks.picture: Three written scene cards: A, a surge recedes, a young calls, the mother reaches the water's edge and a colonist returns it; B, a working colony turns feed into power, ages a cell into a corpse bed, and uses attar; C, a shore outing reads the salt line and gathers root-line goods beside the nursery. Each is a scene proposal, not a staged game.
asks.picture_kind: written thought experiment, not a capture, mock image or staged game
asks.text: Which scene would you put first to decide whether this mod understands you, and what failure there would make you stop?
asks.decision: Flagship pick and first concrete rejection case.
asks.why: F1/F2/F3. Nothing located records a flagship pick. A successful graphic swap or isolated method call cannot select the mod's face for you.
asks.guess: A first. It joins the moving shore to a creature's limitation and a choice only the colony can make. B should be a separate demonstration.
asks.tree_change: The chosen card becomes the first showcase only after a recorded owner pick. Its reject case becomes a core observation. The other cards remain separate candidates/checks; feature proofs and the surge-to-rescue interaction remain required. Root approval alone does not pick a flagship.

asks.title: When the nursery asks too much
asks.picture: A forty-colonist base has several crying young in separate drying pools after a surge. A surgeon is tending fever, haulers are working, and one rescue route crosses a dangerous stretch of roots. The mother cannot do the land crossing for you.
asks.picture_kind: written thought experiment, not a capture, mock image or staged game
asks.text: What would a good rescue effort look like that day, and what loss should still be possible after you make that effort?
asks.decision: Rescue workload, usable time and readable failure at colony scale.
asks.why: F2/F3. The rescue and the possibility of failure are already in scope. Their demands on an ordinary colony are not fixed by a random spawn count or a drying timer.
asks.guess: A real expedition with a few people, rather than every colonist stopping to carry babies; a difficult or delayed rescue can fail, but a prompt prepared party has a useful chance.
asks.tree_change: If a few people should cope, tune pool lifetimes, travel and spawn distribution around that scene and prove it with normal jobs. If it should become a colony emergency, require a visible reason to mobilise and a test of that larger commitment. If triage is the point, require enough information to choose which pool to reach first. No answer invents guaranteed survival or removes the built rescue.

asks.title: What the approaching surge lets you do
asks.picture: The sea starts its long exhale while workers are in the channels and crops stand on unfloored ground. The current incident letter announces a surge as the salt begins its ramp inland. Your existing ruling already says exposed crops in the band die; floors and bridges are the engineering answer.
asks.picture_kind: written thought experiment, not a capture, mock image or staged game
asks.text: By the time the brine reaches that work area, which last-minute preparations should still be possible, and which mistakes should already be too late to undo?
asks.decision: Actionable warning and the boundary between preparation and emergency response.
asks.why: F1/F3. An irregular event can be honest and still allow no useful response. A warning's value is what can be done with it, not that a letter exists.
asks.guess: Recall exposed workers and secure a nearby rescue route; saving an entire badly sited farm requires earlier engineering. The landscape should help explain why the line reached it.
asks.tree_change: If recall is the intended response, add a scene with dispersed workers and an observable recall window. If emergency building should work, test ordinary construction time against the moving front. If the lesson is earlier siting, demonstrate the warning signs before the surge and preserve a fair escape route. Crop death, irregular timing and floor protection stay settled.

asks.title: What rot power earns in an ordinary base
asks.picture: The colony has a steady waste stream, a few decay cells, batteries and other generators. One cell is running low and another is near becoming a rotting bed. Today's raw-food filter does not deliver the already-promised rot feed; that is a code gap, not the choice here.
asks.picture_kind: written thought experiment, not a capture, mock image or staged game
asks.text: What job should those cells do in the base's power supply, and what daily work should earning that power take?
asks.decision: Power's practical role, feed labour and replacement cost; not permission to redefine rot as fresh raw food.
asks.why: F2/F3. A generator can pass an output-number test while it is too feeble to matter or so useful that the delta becomes a fuel chore. The role in colony life sets the tuning.
asks.guess: A useful local contribution from things the colony was throwing away, with hauling and eventual replacement as real costs; enough to plan around without making every other generator pointless.
asks.tree_change: If it is steady supply, require useful ordinary loads over several days with actual feeding and replacement. If it is reserve power, require a meaningful outage scene and an honest way to see the reserve. If it mainly supports a small shoreline workshop, use that scale for the acceptance load. These answers tune output, consumption and lifetime; rot feeding and spent-bed conversion are already owed.

asks.title: Why go back into the roots
asks.picture: After a surge the nearest safe root-line holds a little wood and cloth. Farther along the channel are metal, a brined wreck and a crying young. Travelling there costs a working afternoon and exposure to the delta's predators.
asks.picture_kind: written thought experiment, not a capture, mock image or staged game
asks.text: What would make the longer salvage trip worth planning, and what should the crew be able to judge before setting out?
asks.decision: Salvage reward scale and information sufficient to choose an outing.
asks.why: F2/F3. Loose goods, wrecks and rescue already exist. Without a useful difference between trips, restocking can become free income or busywork. This asks about the existing salvage's value and information.
asks.guess: The short trip keeps the colony supplied; a larger visible find justifies a prepared outing. I would let the crew see enough to estimate the work and danger, without revealing every wreck reward.
asks.tree_change: If salvage is ordinary supply, require recurring useful quantities and reasonable hauling in the routine-colony scene. If the important payoff is occasional wreck recovery, require a recognisable find and an ordinary salvage job with risk and reward. If exploration is meant to reveal the value, make discovery itself readable and test the return trip. Add no auction, appraisal minigame or new quest from the old unchosen pitches.

asks.title: A change worth remembering after the fever
asks.picture: A colonist survives a serious illness here and later returns to ordinary work. The existing tables sometimes give nothing, sometimes a modest lasting change, and very rarely a strange one; you never choose the result. Several promised strange effects are still only partial in code.
asks.picture_kind: written thought experiment, not a capture, mock image or staged game
asks.text: After that survivor goes back to work, what moment would make you feel that the Miasma had left its mark on them?
asks.decision: Player-observable payoff and which existing boon outcomes warrant core experience scenes.
asks.why: F2. The undirected boon table and its named effects are already ruled. The unresolved part is what makes the result felt in play instead of merely adding a line on the health tab.
asks.guess: A small, unmistakable difference in the survivor's ordinary life, with the strange outcomes capable of becoming a memorable story. I would start by showing the effects already specified.
asks.tree_change: If the ordinary effect must be felt, bind acceptance to an actual task or encounter demonstrating the relevant ruled boon, not a hediff count. If a clear health/stat explanation is sufficient for minor effects, keep those as cheaper checks and reserve scenes for the strange outcomes. If only some effects matter to the root, give those core observations and keep the rest covered as built functionality. No answer adds a selectable boon, genes or a new medical economy.

asks.title: How much life fits before the mother dies
asks.picture: The colony meets a visibly ancient mother, returns young through several surges, and some young choose to stay with it. Eventually she dies and a much smaller juvenile takes the watch. Your existing ruling already requires clear foreshadowing and a child successor, with no adult growth arc.
asks.picture_kind: written thought experiment, not a capture, mock image or staged game
asks.text: What should the colony have had time to do with her before that death, and where in an ordinary playthrough should that handover fall?
asks.decision: Relationship/death pacing in campaign play, under the already-ruled juvenile ending.
asks.why: F2/F3. Age art is built and historically proved, but an elder stage and life expectancy do not establish a satisfying campaign-length relationship. This asks about pace, not whether she dies or whether the child inherits.
asks.guess: Enough ordinary play for repeated rescues and a relationship, then the handover within a campaign the player is likely to reach. Neither an immediate farewell nor a wait for the juvenile to grow into a sea giant.
asks.tree_change: If it should happen in the first settled season, test meeting, several opportunities to act and foreshadowed death within that span. If it belongs to a longer-established base, set the accepted encounter age/pace from that picture and test a finite ordinary-play horizon. If exact timing does not matter, keep no additional timing leaf, while retaining foreshadowing and real juvenile guarding. Every branch still needs the missing guard transfer; no full-grown successor is inferred.

contradictions.text: Shared ownership settled: EnvironmentalHazards owns axis/surge/pools/exposure/boons/anchor, Miasma owns content and its local loops; FlowWorks owns fluid terrain/canals; CreatureBehaviors owns vermin pressure. No duplicate engine proposed.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Pollination gate is cut, succession retained, Nine rites later. Older roster/spec/walk language is not today's scope or a reason to ask again.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Latest suite result partial; aged-render PASS and September wander/training/predation proofs are historical. Raw latest logs and matching fingerprints unavailable.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Surge applies a scalar change and water-grade/crust repaint; no new water footprint is created here. DetectPools later analyses existing water connectivity. Natural causal surge-to-orphans proof must distinguish this from prepainted ponds or direct-spawn helpers.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: PruneOccupants does not test leaving pool cells or rescue ownership; fallback destroys every still-spawned tracked occupant without location/faction check. A log is also not a player-visible departure sign.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Promote only chooses/saves an heir and messages; it never assigns an anchor/duty or smaller guard radius. This does not deliver the already-ruled guarding child.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: CheckReturns takes the first in-reach mother, ignoring young's crèche; TryReturn can update that mother while NoteReturned resolves a different marker. Distance/water does not prove connected water or biological ownership.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Return removes the hediff containing self-tame/creche link then removes young from registered list. A normal return is not currently an end-to-end demonstration that a rescued young later self-tames and inherits.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: FoodRaw feed filter does not express the accepted rotting-goods/spoiled-meals/corpses supply. Direct Refuel(float) proof bypasses selection and delivery of actual feed items.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Balm reduces any first permanent Hediff_Injury's severity, potentially changing injury pain/function; cosmetic-only and no-medicine scope is stronger than fresh-wound untouched. Needs engine-state proof or correction under existing authority.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: peakSeverity is tracked but no CompExposeData persists it. Reload late in recovery can forget that the pawn previously exceeded the required peak; a boon result is gated by that forgotten state.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Water-cell checks neither require sea-connected components nor prevent land segments between valid water destinations. Keep the already-ruled connection/no-land promise; build/proof gap rather than an owner fork.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Pallasheen castings-only germination, quennath host adjacency and broad fresh/brine flora/fauna sorting were not found in present plain fertility defs. Plant fed-state art also remains distinct from generic feeding mote.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: mangal_gated_on_swarm still reports UNMEASURED for deliberately removed functionality. DEFAULTS/NEW also omit the built lastvineRearingEnabled setting. The walk's NEVER RUN LIVE is contradicted by recorded later live runs.

contradictions.speaker: agent
contradictions.text: Distinct aged art is built and historically observed. No special measured age slowdown, stated remaining lifetime, NPC warning or campaign death pace was located; art alone does not establish all September foreshadowing promises.

failure_modes: F1: The moving shore is a recolour rather than the promised changing nursery: a surge never actually cuts off young, salt history cannot be read, or the mother's water boundary is bypassed by paths/canals. Sources: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md; design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/miasma_fauna_roster_2026-09-23.md; src/RimMandrake/EnvironmentalHazards/Source/RM_GradientAxisRepaint.cs.

F2: Hope has no playable consequence: rescue/sale changes the wrong mother, the heir is only an inspect label, rot power is really fresh-food fuel, or beauty and survival rewards exist mainly in descriptions. Sources: ITEM:MIASMA_MOTHERS_PRICE_1; OWNER:1790981774745786745; src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Source/RM_WardenMotherSuccession.cs.

F3: The crowded delta becomes an unfair chore or loses its state: cries and jobs churn at colony scale, saved progress differs after reload, a saved/rescued young vanishes, or the proof script passes helper calls while the actual player loop is untested. Sources: src/RimMandrake/Miasma/validation.py; src/RimMandrake/EnvironmentalHazards/Source/RM_MapComponent_StrandingPools.cs; src/RimMandrake/Miasma/Source/RM_MapComponent_YoungCall.cs.

failure_mode_sources.text: Changing shore, readable geography and water-bound nursery.
Consequences, useful rot and earned continuity.
Playable scale, persistence and proof honesty.

neighbours.text: Axis/repaint/surge, pools, exposure/weather, boons, anchor/water lock/despoil memory. Shared switches live there; Miasma provides data and consumes the recede signal.
Brackish/brine grades and canals; Miasma must honour water connectivity without a second hydrology engine. Sea-connected swimming is an integration obligation, not established by a wet cell.
Vermin breeder, shared population/pressure and replenishment; kills alter actual live pawn counts, not a separate Miasma population ledger.
Free juveniles and adults. The rich nursery already has source defs there; no new juvenile species commissioned.
Wreck families/weathering/salvage engine; Miasma supplies brined frame/tank and field selection. Distinct from its loose flotsam restock.
Shared RM_Bones resource; Miasma corpse processing creates it. Not a second local bone definition.
Optional cooking ingredient from spent beds, required by the owner's existing typed ruling; cooking and pantry systems stay Cuisine's.
Additive cast and campaign buyer names; a free-biome read alone misses these. No tier/canon or eviction ruling invented.
Guarded nearby conversion/weird-food and several animal abilities/regeneration. A guarded comp's XML presence does not establish its live behaviour.

Predator hunting, hauling/storage, power nets, trader caravan arrivals, training, skull provenance and analysis/research already perform parts of the job. Test those actual player paths rather than duplicate them.

neighbours.owner: Direct Sun / Sun and Shade / tree shade
neighbours.text: Ordinary ambient heat plus geometry-based Direct Sun remain the standing rule. No bespoke Miasma heat kind; canopy shade and heat tests belong to the shared system.
Shared everyday/explosive growth is already folded; population/forest pace must be judged under the intended composed runtime, not hand-tuned against a fictitious isolated plant system.
